committed_findings.summary: The proof’s numerical statements consistently identify their counted objects: members, point incidences, closed meeting neighbors, completions and key fibers. Direct arithmetic checks reproduce the stated contradictions. The diagnostic counts also agree with their reported objects without supporting an additional universal theorem. No exposition revision is required.

checks.method: Read frozen Sections 3–4 and recomputed the incidence, meeting-neighborhood, census and fiber bounds in Python using exact integers. Checked feasible integer q from 0 through 12 in the two displayed incidence constraints.
checks.observation: The incidence inequalities permit at most m=40; 9·168=1512<37·41=1517. Profile A’s residual incidences total 12·14+4·19=244=4·61. An H2 row has degree sum 66, hence at most 52 closed meeting neighbors and at least nine disjoint completions. The census then gives n2≥24, while five keys with at most four outsider pairs each give n2≤20. Each transition refers to the appropriate family or incidence count.
checks.scope: Arithmetic-to-object correspondence in the two profile exclusions

checks.method: Parsed the two frozen diagnostic outputs and recalculated the candidate-space size and histogram total; compared the numerical interpretation with Section 6. This did not rerun the full geometry enumeration.
checks.observation: C(28,4)=20,475, both histograms agree and sum to 156,960, and the reported residual maximum five suggests total 40+5=45. Section 6 identifies those as normalized finite diagnostics and expressly leaves normalization and the universal45 theorem unestablished. These checks support reporting accuracy, not proof coverage.
checks.scope: Diagnostic cardinalities and assurance wording

committed_findings.summary: Exact arithmetic and degenerate-case checks confirm the integer rounding, closed-neighborhood correction, nonempty H2 choice and final graph-fiber cap. The inequalities alone permit m=40 at q=9, so the manuscript appropriately concludes eighty without promoting the stronger45 diagnostic. No correction is required.

checks.method: Run scratch/alpha/round05_arithmetic.py to enumerate all integral q in 0..12 and m in 0..99 satisfying the two displayed inequalities; check the exact elimination arithmetic. Larger m are already excluded by 2m≤9q≤108.
checks.observation: The maximum feasible m is40, attained numerically only at q=9. The displayed cancellation gives37m≤1512 and floor(1512/37)=40, with37·41=1517. Empty overlap correctly forces m=0. This verifies the bound and shows that these incidence inequalities do not establish cap45 or attainability of any family.
checks.scope: Two-star threshold and incidence robustness

checks.method: Independently evaluate the closed-neighborhood bounds, enumerate nonnegative census solutions, and enumerate all64 simple graphs on four outsider points in scratch/alpha/round05_arithmetic.py.
checks.observation: The +2 correction gives meeting caps57 and52 and hence nine disjoint completions for an H2 row. Before using that row, the census already forces n2≥15, so its selection is noncircular. Adding n0≥9 leaves exactly(9,28,24),(10,26,25),(11,24,26),(12,22,27) for(n0,n1,n2). Every four-vertex graph with maximum degree≤2 has at most four edges; combining five keys with this cap gives20<24.

committed_findings.summary: Exact integer checks confirm the bound forty residual members and the two auxiliary bounds of four used in Profile A. A deliberate relaxation shows why the inherited at-most-two-high-points theorem matters: replacing residual caps fourteen/nine by fifteen/ten permits forty-five in the scalar model. The manuscript uses the stronger justified caps and does not mistake scalar feasibility for actual-family realizability.

checks.method: Independently enumerate q=0,...,12 and m=0,...,61 satisfying 2m≤9q and 3m≤14(12−q)+9q; repeat with degree caps fifteen and ten. Retain executable arithmetic in scratch/beta/round05_bounds.py.
checks.observation: The exact caps allow maximum m=40, only at q=9. Directly, m=41 would force q≥10 from overlap incidence and q≤9 from U incidence. Relaxed caps permit m=45,q=9, confirming that the proof needs the inherited high-point restriction to obtain the residual degree cap fourteen rather than fifteen. This is an auxiliary scalar calculation; it asserts no family with m=40 or m=45 exists.
checks.scope: Integer margins and robustness of the two-star incidence bound

checks.method: Enumerate all subfamilies of the five edges of C5 for pairwise intersection, and all sixty-four graphs on four labeled vertices for the actual three-edge sunflower predicate; compare with Sections 4.2 and 4.3.
checks.observation: An intersecting C5 edge family has at most two edges, so the two coordinate projections allow at most four distinct completions. A three-sunflower-free graph on four vertices has at most four edges; exactly three labeled maximal four-edge families occur, each a four-cycle. Thus the separate completion and outsider-fiber bounds are exact for their auxiliary graph hypotheses. These checks corroborate the prose argument without claiming a new formal proof.
checks.scope: Small auxiliary combinatorial caps in Profile A
